supplier_excerpts.excerpt:
Let $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the Laurent polynomial ring and let
$\Lambda:=A[z]=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ be the polynomial ring over $A$ in one
indeterminate ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). For $n\ge1$ let
$H(n):=\Lambda\otimes_AH_v(n)$ be the scalar extension of the generic type-A
Hecke algebra of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), so that $H(n)$ is the unital
$\Lambda$-algebra with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
and $H(1)=\Lambda$. The $\Lambda$-algebra $H(n)$ is free with basis
$\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$, where $T_w$ is the product of the generators along a reduced
word ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-symmetric-group]]).

The generators induce a $\Lambda$-algebra homomorphism
$\iota_n:H(n)\to H(n+1)$, $T_i\mapsto T_i$; it is injective, so we identify
$H(n)$ with its image, a $\Lambda$-subalgebra of $H(n+1)$.

A **Markov trace on the type-A Hecke tower** is a family of $\Lambda$-linear
maps $\operatorname{tr}_n:H(n)\to\Lambda$, $n\ge1$, such that

- (M1) $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$ for one (equivalently, by (M2), every) $n$;
- (M2) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}\circ\iota_n=\operatorname{tr}_n$ for all $n\ge1$;
- (M3) $\operatorname{tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{tr}_n(yx)$ for all $x,y\in H(n)$;
- (M4) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(x\,T_n)=z\,\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$ for all $n\ge1$
  and $x\in H(n)$.

Here $z\in\Lambda$ is a formal parameter, distinct from the Hecke parameter $v$;
no value of $z$ is fixed or inverted by this definition, and the trace takes
values in $\Lambda$, not in a field.

**Caveats.** This is a family over the whole tower, not a single functional; the
conditions (M1)--(M4) are a definition, so no trace is asserted to exist here
(existence and uniqueness is
[[thm-the-ocneanu-markov-trace-exists-and-is-unique]]). By (M3), (M4) is
equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(u\,T_n\,v)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(uv)$ for
all $u,v\in H(n)$: applied to $uT_nv$ one gets
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(uT_nv)=\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(T_nvu)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(vu)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(uv)$,
and conversely take $v=1$.

Let $H(1)\subset H(2)\subset\cdots$ be the type-A Hecke tower over
$\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of [[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]].
Then there exists a unique Markov trace $(\operatorname{tr}_n)_{n\ge1}$ on this
tower in the sense of [[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]]. Moreover
it satisfies, for all $n\ge1$, all $x,y\in H(n)$ and all $1\le i\le n-1$:

- (a) $\operatorname{tr}_n(T_i)=z$;
- (b) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_ny)=z\,\operatorname{tr}_n(xy)$;
- (c) $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is determined by (M1)--(M4) alone; it takes values in
  $\Lambda$ and is computed by iterating (b) along the free basis of
  [[lem-the-hecke-tower-is-free-over-the-previous-level]].

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\delta\in R$, and use the noncrossing-pairing diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], with the left factor stacked above the right factor. For a basis diagram $D:n\to n$, close each top endpoint to the corresponding bottom endpoint outside the rectangle and let $c(D)$ be the number of circles in the resulting finite graph. Define

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$$

and extend $R$-linearly to $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. This is the **unnormalized closure trace**. In particular, $\operatorname{Tr}_0(1_0)=1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_n(1_n)=\delta^n$. No unit or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is required.

Let $\cup:0\to2$ and $\cap:2\to0$ be the standard cup and cap in the diagram category. For $n\ge1$ define the **right partial trace** by

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(x)=(1_{n-1}\otimes\cap)\circ(x\otimes1_1)\circ(1_{n-1}\otimes\cup),\qquad x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

It is a map $\mathrm{TL}_n\to\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$. If $\delta$ is a unit, define $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. This agrees with the normalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] over $\mathbb C$ when $\delta\ne0$.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. For each $n\ge0$, let $F_n:=R\langle u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}\rangle$ be the free associative unital $R$-algebra on the indicated symbols ([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]). When $n=0$ or $n=1$, the symbol set is empty and $F_n=R$.

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by

$$u_i^2-\delta u_i\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad u_i u_j-u_j u_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$

and

$$u_i u_{i+1}u_i-u_i,\qquad u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}-u_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2).$$

The abstract **rank-$n$ Temperley–Lieb algebra** is the presented $R$-algebra

$$P_n(R,\delta):=F_n/I_n.$$

Thus its defining relations are $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ for $|i-j|>1$. The definition of a presented $R$-algebra and its universal property are those of [[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]].

Let $H(1)\subset H(2)\subset\cdots$ be the Hecke tower of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]], with $H(n)$ free of rank $n!$
over $\Lambda$ with basis $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]), and for
$1\le i\le n$ put $w^{(i)}:=s_ns_{n-1}\cdots s_{n-i+1}$, $w^{(0)}:=1$. Then for
every $n\ge1$:

1. $H(n+1)$ is a free left $H(n)$-module with basis
   $T_{w^{(0)}},T_{w^{(1)}},\dots,T_{w^{(n)}}$: every element of $H(n+1)$ has a
   unique expression $\sum_{i=0}^{n}x_iT_{w^{(i)}}$ with $x_i\in H(n)$;
2. $H(n+1)$ is also a free right $H(n)$-module with basis
   $T_{(w^{(0)})^{-1}},T_{(w^{(1)})^{-1}},\dots,T_{(w^{(n)})^{-1}}$;
3. the  $H(n)$-sub-bimodule $H(n)T_nH(n)$ equals the direct sum
   $\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}H(n)T_{w^{(i)}}$, and the multiplication map
   $$H(n)\otimes_{H(n-1)}H(n)\longrightarrow H(n+1),\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto xT_ny,$$
   is an isomorphism of $H(n)$-bimodules onto $H(n)T_nH(n)$; consequently
   $H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$ holds as a direct sum of $H(n)$-bimodules in
   the form $H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus\bigl(H(n)\otimes_{H(n-1)}H(n)\bigr)$. All three parts are proved here. Each chosen nonidentity minimal left-coset representative $w^{(i)}$
   has a displayed reduced expression containing $s_n$ exactly once; this does
   not characterize all basis elements whose reduced expressions contain
   $s_n$ once. In the tensor notation of part (3), set $H(0):=\Lambda$, the
   scalar extension $\Lambda\otimes_AH_v(0)$, so the $n=1$ case is defined.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the link-invariance assertion below, via
[[thm-the-hecke-trace-construction-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]] and its
Markov-equivalence supplier. Let $H(1)\subset H(2)\subset\cdots$ be the Hecke tower over
$\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]], with $H(n)$ generated by
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For $1\le i\le
n-2$ let
$$E^{(i)}_n:=\sum_{w\in\langle s_i,s_{i+1}\rangle}T_w$$
be the sum of the six standard-basis elements over the parabolic subgroup
$\langle s_i,s_{i+1}\rangle\cong S_3$ inside $H(n)$, and let $J(n)\subset H(n)$
be the two-sided ideal generated by the elements $E^{(i)}_n$ for
$1\le i\le n-2$ ([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]]). The **Temperley--Lieb
quotient** of the Hecke tower is the quotient algebra
$$\mathrm{TL}(n):=H(n)/J(n)$$
([[def-quotient-ring]]). Put $D:=\Lambda[(v+1)^{-1}]$ and form
$H_D(n):=D\otimes_\Lambda H(n)$ and
$\mathrm{TL}_D(n):=D\otimes_\Lambda\mathrm{TL}(n)$. The normalized generators
below are defined in these scalar extensions, where $v+1$ is a unit.

**The Temperley--Lieb relations.** In $H_D(n)$ put
$$e_i:=\frac{T_i+1}{v+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-1),\qquad \lambda:=\frac{v}{(v+1)^2}.$$
Then $e_i^2=e_i$ and $e_ie_j=e_je_i$ for $|i-j|>1$, while in the quotient
$\mathrm{TL}_D(n)$ one has
$$e_ie_{i+1}e_i=\lambda e_i,\qquad e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=\lambda e_{i+1} \qquad(1\le i\le n-2).$$
These are Jones' Temperley--Lieb relations
$e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_{i\pm1}e_i=\lambda e_i$, $e_ie_j=e_je_i$ for $|i-j|>1$
with loop parameter $\lambda$. After adjoining $s$ with $s^2=v$ to $D$, the
elements $f_i:=(v+1)s^{-1}e_i=\lambda^{-1/2}e_i$ satisfy
$$f_i^2=\delta f_i,\qquad f_if_{i+1}f_i=f_i,\qquad f_{i+1}f_if_{i+1}=f_{i+1},\qquad f_if_j=f_jf_i\ (|i-j|>1),$$
with $\delta:=\lambda^{-1/2}=\frac{v+1}{v^{1/2}}=s+s^{-1}$ when $s^2=v$.

**The Jones specialization.** Let
$z_0:=-\frac{1}{v+1}$ and let
$$T:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},(v+1)^{-1},s]\Big/\bigl(s^2-v\bigr)$$
be the ring in which $v+1$ is inverted and a square root $s$ of $v$ is
adjoined. By the universal property of the coefficient ring
$R$ of [[def-the-homflypt-coefficient-ring]] there is a unique unital ring
homomorphism $\varphi:R\to T$ with
$$v\mapsto v,\qquad z\mapsto z_0,\qquad s\mapsto s,\qquad u\mapsto s ;$$
it sends $\alpha=(uz)^{-1}\mapsto-\frac{s^2+1}{s}$. The **Jones
specialization** of the invariant $P$ of
[[def-homflypt-polynomial-from-the-hecke-markov-trace]] is
$$V(\widehat\beta):=\varphi\bigl(P(\widehat\beta)\bigr) =s^{e(\beta)}\Bigl(-\frac{s^2+1}{s}\Bigr)^{n-1} \operatorname{tr}_n\bigl(\pi_n(\beta)\bigr)\Big|_{z=z_0}\in T$$
for $\beta\in B_n$ with $n\ge1$ and closure $\widehat\beta$
([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]). Then $V$ is an invariant of nonempty oriented links with $V(\text{unknot})=1$ and
$$s^{-2}V(L_+)-s^{2}V(L_-)=(s-s^{-1})V(L_0)$$
on every skein triple; in the variable $t:=s^2$ this is the Jones skein
relation $t^{-1}V_+-tV_-=(t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2})V_0$, and $V$ is the Jones
polynomial in the convention of Birman--Brendle §4.3 property 6: positive $\sigma_1^3$ has value $t+t^3-t^4$. Mirroring a link replaces $t$ by $t^{-1}$; the convention is fixed, rather than chosen separately for each computation. The separate empty-link extension of $P$ specializes to $V(\varnothing)=-s/(s^2+1)$ in $T$; that formal extension is outside the classical Jones-polynomial identification for nonempty links.

**Caveats.** The quotient $\mathrm{TL}(n)$ is defined over $\Lambda$, but the
normalized generators and their displayed relations are in the base change
$\mathrm{TL}_D(n)$, since $v+1$ need not be a unit in $\Lambda$. No claim is
made here that the Ocneanu trace on $H(n)$ factors through the quotient map
$H(n)\to\mathrm{TL}(n)$; the quotient is recorded for the Temperley--Lieb
relations (1), and the Jones invariant is defined as the specialization of the
link invariant $P$, not as a trace on the quotient. What
is proved below is the Markov normalization after scalar extension, namely
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}^+(xe_n)=\frac{z+1}{v+1}\operatorname{tr}_n^+(x)$ for
$x\in H_D(n)$, whose value at $z_0$ is $\lambda$; this is Jones' Markov trace
normalization for the Temperley--Lieb parameter $\tau=\lambda$. The
identification of $V$ with the Jones polynomial uses the explicit Hecke-trace specialization in Birman--Brendle §4.3 property 6, quoted in [F6]. That source also supplies the relation on arbitrary oriented skein triples; the local skein supplier proves the braided triples.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1_{n-\ell+1}$ for $n\ge\ell-1$, and $I_n=0$ below that rank. Then $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$, and $\mathrm{TL}_n/I_n$ is the direct sum of full matrix algebras with multiplicities given by length-$n$ paths from $0$ of heights $0,\ldots,\ell-2$. The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. The highest-weight-$2$ channel is retained only when $\ell\ge4$. Pivotal traces, twists and all framed ribbon closures agree under the stated corrected comparison.
